definition: The average monthly recurring revenue an MSP earns per supported user seat, across every managed services client. It folds all recurring services into one per-user figure.
Money clients owe you for work or services already invoiced and not yet paid. It sits on the balance sheet as an asset until it is collected.
An all-you-can-eat agreement bundles unlimited support for a fixed monthly fee, with no per-ticket or per-hour billing for work inside its scope.

A business associate agreement is the contract a healthcare client must have with you before you touch anything containing patient information, setting out what you may do with it and what you owe them if it leaks.
The percentage of a technician's available working hours that are logged against client work. Available hours exclude holidays and approved leave.
BYOD is an arrangement where staff use personal phones, tablets or laptops to do company work, rather than being issued equipment the business owns.
The total sales and marketing spend in a period divided by the number of new clients won in it. It is what one new client actually cost you to win.

CASL means Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation. It regulates commercial electronic messages and also covers activities such as installing computer programs, so an MSP should check both its marketing practices and its software deployment arrangements.

CMMC is the American defense department's framework for proving that a contractor handling sensitive but unclassified government information has the security controls it claims, verified at intervals rather than asserted.
Co-managed IT is an arrangement where an MSP works alongside a client's internal IT staff rather than replacing them, with responsibilities split by agreement rather than by default.
The share of post-ticket survey responses that rate the support experience positively. It measures how clients felt about individual interactions with the service desk.
The average number of days between sending an invoice and receiving payment. It measures how quickly billed revenue turns into cash.
How long an attacker is inside an environment before being detected. It runs from the first compromise to the moment someone notices it.
Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization. It approximates the operating profit a business produces, independent of how it is financed or taxed.

EDR is software on endpoints that watches process and system behavior, records it, and allows an operator to investigate and respond (isolating a machine or killing a process) rather than only blocking known-bad files.
The NPS question asked of your own staff: how likely are you to recommend this company as a place to work. Promoters minus detractors, from minus 100 to plus 100.
First contact resolution is the share of tickets resolved in the initial interaction, without escalation, a callback, or a second touch.
Revenue minus the direct cost of delivering it, such as technician labor, tools and resold product, expressed as a percentage of revenue.
The share of last year's recurring revenue from existing clients that you kept, counting cancellations and downgrades but ignoring any expansion. It can never exceed 100 percent.
HIPAA is the American health-privacy law that decides how patient information must be protected, and it reaches you directly the moment you provide IT services to anyone who holds that information.
ITIL is a published framework of IT service management practices (incident, problem, change and service request handling among them), used as a common vocabulary and a starting structure.

IT service management is the practice of running IT as a set of defined services with owners, processes and agreed levels, rather than as a queue of requests handled however whoever picks them up prefers.
The number of clients who ended their agreement in a period, as a percentage of the clients you had at the start of it. It counts clients, not dollars.
The total gross margin a typical client produces over the whole time they stay with you. It is usually estimated as monthly gross margin per client times average client lifetime in months.

MDR is detection and response delivered as a service, where an external team monitors the tooling, triages what it produces, and responds, rather than the software being handed over for someone in-house to watch.
A sign-in that needs two or more kinds of proof, such as a password plus a code from an app or a hardware key. A stolen password alone is then not enough to get in.
Monthly recurring revenue is the predictable, contracted revenue an MSP bills every month, counted separately from project work, hardware resale and hourly labor.
A loyalty score from one question: how likely are you to recommend us, on a scale of 0 to 10. It is the percentage of promoters (9 or 10) minus the percentage of detractors (0 to 6).
The recurring revenue your existing clients pay today as a percentage of what the same clients paid a year ago, counting expansion, price increases, downgrades and cancellations.

PHIPA is Ontario's Personal Health Information Protection Act. It governs personal health information handled by health information custodians and sets obligations for their agents and electronic service providers.

PIPEDA is Canada's federal private-sector privacy law for personal information handled in commercial activities. Its full name is the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act. Provincial and sector-specific laws affect which rules apply.
PSA is the system an MSP runs its business in: tickets, time entry, contracts, billing and reporting, ideally connected to the tooling that generates the work.
A quarterly business review is a scheduled meeting between an MSP and a client to review service delivery, discuss the client's business direction, and plan the technology work that follows from it.

Quebec Law 25 is a privacy reform that amended Quebec's personal-information laws. For private businesses, the operative duties sit in the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector as amended.
RMM is the software an MSP uses to monitor client endpoints and servers, apply patches, run scripts and access machines remotely, usually through an agent installed on each device.
The most data, measured in time, the business can afford to lose in a failure. An RPO of four hours means backups must run at least every four hours.
The longest a system can be down after a failure before the outage becomes unacceptable to the business. It sets how fast a restore has to be.
A service level agreement is the part of a contract that states what response and resolution a client is entitled to, usually by severity, and what happens when you miss it.
SOC 2 is an audit report in which an independent firm examines how you handle security, availability and confidentiality, and states whether your controls did what you said they did.
Time to first response is how long a client waits between raising a ticket and hearing from a human who has read it.
Time to resolution is how long a ticket takes from being raised to the underlying issue being fixed, measured end to end rather than by how long anyone worked on it.
A vCIO is someone who provides technology strategy to a client that has no CIO of its own: planning, budgeting, risk and roadmap rather than support and remediation.
XDR extends endpoint detection by correlating signals from other layers (identity, email, cloud services, network) so that related events are assessed together rather than as separate alerts.

Zero trust is a security approach that verifies every request on its own merits (who is asking, from what device, for what) instead of granting access because the request came from inside the network.
